title_original: Best Films of 2025
editorial_title_zh: 2025年最佳电影
editorial_excerpt_zh: 敲鼓请进：《电影评论》2025年度影评人投票结果现已揭晓！在本页中，你将看到我们的20部最佳电影榜单，其中附有影评人的原创赏析及更多内容。

Telaroli）的最佳修复电影榜单、影评人兼编辑加文·史密斯（Gavin Smith）的年度最佳经典重映榜单，以及德维卡·吉里什（Devika Girish）撰写的最佳场景和迈克尔·科雷斯基（Michael Koresky）撰写的最佳表演文章。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "立即订阅《电影评论》快讯——这是掌握我们所有2025年度最佳报道的最佳途径。", "links": [{"text": "Subscribe", "url": "https://www.filmcomment.com/newsletter-sign-up/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "声称《血战到底》（One Battle After Another）将角色简化为漫画式讽刺的人，误读了这部电影所剖析的本质：忠诚的机制。在一段夸张的序幕之后，保罗·托马斯·安德森（Paul Thomas Anderson）标志性的宏大叙事跳跃了16年，跟随糊涂的前革命者鲍勃·弗格森（Bob Ferguson，莱昂纳多·迪卡普里奥饰），他如今带着混血十几岁的女儿薇拉（钱斯·因芬蒂饰，光芒四射）隐姓埋名地生活。随后，白人至上主义者洛克乔上校（肖恩·潘饰）——尽管身不由己，他对黑人女性却情有独钟，尤其是薇拉的母亲佩菲迪亚·贝弗利·希尔斯（特亚娜·泰勒饰）——找上门来对付这个少女。鲍勃被迫重操旧业，在前战友和薇拉的空手道教练塞尔吉奥（本尼西奥·德·托罗饰，全身心投入）的帮助下追踪女儿。影片中由偏旁驱动、脉搏般跳动的动作场面展示的不是意识形态，而是效忠的基础设施——维系任何深陷困境的集体所需的信号、行话、计划和团结。薇拉在目睹了所有的双重背叛、怀疑和牺牲之后，依然选择加入这项事业——这确实是一个值得拯救的信息。——艾比·孙（Abby Sun）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影中充满了各种倒霉的准罪犯，他们的周密计划最终落空，但凯莉·雷查德（Kelly Reichardt）的《主谋》（The Mastermind）中J·B·穆尼（乔什·奥康纳饰）策划的抢劫，却是史上最糟糕的计划之一。穆尼只是在自己的想象中是个大师，他在没有意识到这一点的情况下，耗尽了自己的唯一资产——魅力。他备受冷落的妻子（阿拉娜·哈伊姆）和两个孩子、退休法官父亲（比尔·坎普）以及俱乐部名媛母亲（霍普·戴维斯）都曾纵容过他，但他的时间已经不多了。值得注意的是，这部电影以70年代为背景，那是一个社会行动主义盛行（J.B.对此不感兴趣）、更容易拒绝长大的时期。他在某个时刻打电话给妻子，说他所做的一切都是为了这个家庭——或者说，“四分之三”为了家庭。仅说它是反类型片是不够的；它是对银幕上罕见的一种人物的极其原创的视角，因为这里的兴趣在于缺席而非在场。《主谋》是一个喜剧恐怖故事，讲述了一个彻头彻尾的虚空之人，既无法自我认知，也无法改变。——莫莉·哈斯凯尔（Molly Haskell）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "小克莱伯·门东萨（Kleber Mendonça Filho）是一位将电影视为如同呼吸般不可或缺的电影人，由他来打造一部既浸润于经典电影灵感的技巧、又饱含20世纪70年代巴西日常生活氛围与质感的政治惊悚片，再合适不过了。《秘密特工》（The Secret Agent）采用宽银幕泛欧视觉（Panavision）摄影，并融入了德帕玛风格的分光镜镜头、奥特曼式的变焦以及直取《星球大战》的擦除转场，充满了完美契合时代的细节，并由瓦格纳·莫拉（Wagner Moura）深情演绎了一位陷入巴西军事独裁血腥风暴中的科学家兼父亲，以此将整部电影凝聚在一起。但这也是一部不断漫游的电影——正如一个角色所说，“有点即兴，巴西风格”。门东萨着迷于电影的历史和工具如何成为一个档案；电影在其认为任何其他电影人都可能会从记录中删去的、所有所谓不必要的额外生活细节中，找到了最震撼的画面和道德良知。——迈克尔·布莱尔（Michael Blair）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在贾法·帕纳西（Jafar Panahi）的最新力作中，汽车修理工瓦希德（瓦希德·莫巴塞里饰）在纠结是否要杀死那个他几乎可以确定曾在狱中折磨过他的人。瓦希德并非王子，但他的困境——以及帕纳西的这部公路电影——让我想起了《哈姆雷特》，尤其是《捕鼠器》，那是哈姆雷特委托演出的一出戏，旨在证明他的叔叔犯有谋杀罪。“喜剧性的悲剧”是《捕鼠器》所追求的效果，这也是对《这只是一场意外》（It Was Just an Accident）及其核心意象的完美类型界定——一辆卡车，后车厢里装着一个棺材般的盒子，里面躺着一个半清醒的男人。瓦希德开着这辆车在德黑兰四处转悠，接载乘客，希望他们能帮他决定，杀死一个杀人犯是否能改变他的人生或他们依然深爱的国家。在帕纳西刑满释放仅仅一年多后，在无拍摄许可的情况下勉强拍完，这部电影是帕纳西和他的团队一致同意冒的一次险；你在每一秒都能感受到他们向强权讲真话的意志。毫不意外，这份实至名归的赞誉也为帕纳西赢得了缺席判刑。——艾米·陶宾（Amy Taubin）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在一个不断变化的世界里，究竟有什么是可以紧紧抓住的？《风流一代》将这个问题悬而未决。影片的故事背景设定在中国21世纪初的经济转型期，这也是贾樟柯职业生涯长期聚焦的主题。在这里，他的目光转向了内部：他重新利用了早期电影中的素材，构建了一个气势恢宏的故事，讲述了巧巧（赵涛饰）与斌哥（李竹斌饰）之间破碎的浪漫关系。电台广播串联起了一个个历史时刻，比如中国赢得2008年奥运会主办权的那一刻。然而天高皇帝远：贾樟柯更关注的是这片不断变迁的土地上发生的事、人们奔涌向前的步伐，尤其是赵涛脸上掠过的那些神情。在影片的最后三分之一中，她戴着一张几乎遮住整张脸、只露出双眸的面具。但那是怎样的一双眼睛啊——充满渴望与探寻，它们注视着已经变得面目全非的斌哥，一个和他的祖国一样躁动不安的男人。——吉纳维芙·于（Genevieve Yue）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "秘鲁斗牛士安德烈斯·罗卡·雷伊（Andrés Roca Rey）面部扭曲成一个令人联想起哈珀·马克斯（Harpo Marx）式的痛苦怪相，死死盯着一头嘴巴微张、步履踉跄、正快速走向死亡的公牛。他身穿传统的烫金斗牛服（即“光芒战衣”，traje de luces），身上沾满鲜血与斗牛场底部的尘土，他弓起脊背、挺起胸膛，这种男子气概的姿态夸张得近乎抽象。在阿尔伯特·塞拉（Albert Serra）的首部剧情纪录片《太阳之午》中，那架四处游走、深入探究的摄影机向我们展示：这些仪式不过是一层脚手架，本身毫无意义，斗牛士只是将自己的一生悬挂其上。塞拉在罗卡·雷伊的脸上徒劳地寻找着一丝自我认知，或者哪怕一点点意识到自己的人生本质上不过是一头被牵出来表演中世纪荣誉戏剧的动物的迹象。影片暗示，人与野兽之间的界限，就像罗卡·雷伊在又一场残酷而成功的斗牛赛结束后扯下的那些沾满人血与牛血、已经破损的白色氨纶面料一样脆弱。——克林顿·克鲁特（Clinton Krute）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿兰·吉罗迪（Alain Guiraudie）这部淘气的警匪片中并没有真正的性爱，但欲望的力量却穿梭于影片的生命线中，导向一种独特的狡黠与悬疑结局。影片跟随一个英俊的流浪汉（菲利克斯·基西尔饰）回到他风景如画的乡村老家，随着他身边形形色色的人——不分年龄、性别与职业——全都被卷入他的轨道，一张潜藏着地下冲动的狡诈之网也随之徐徐展开，引发了一场场从温柔到带有一丝谋杀意味的神秘邂逅。《圣洁》中的省份背景（吉罗迪的故乡、位于法国南部的奥克西塔尼）、弥漫的感官性欲以及夹杂着羞耻感的不安，延续了这位导演一贯的经典主题。然而，这部电影在他的作品序列中也显得格外耀眼，它对情绪与类型的精湛融合拿捏得炉火纯青，在闹剧与哲学之间自如切换，恰如秋风中随风飘舞的落叶般优雅而变幻莫测。——比阿特丽斯·洛亚萨（Beatrice Loayza）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "曾执导2019年《防火》的加利西亚导演再次回到摩洛哥——他那部充满神秘色彩的《含羞草》（2016）的拍摄地。与那部电影一样，《西拉特》也是一部公路片，讲述了道路走到尽头、沙漠以及不可预测的命运接管一切的地方。塞尔吉·洛佩斯（Sergi López）饰演一个寻找女儿的父亲，他与一群由经验丰富的锐舞老兵组成的“另类家庭”（由一群坚毅真实的非职业演员饰演）走到了一起。凭借其大胆的叙事震惊战术和震撼的电子乐配乐，拉克塞的最新力作堪称21世纪版本的《恐惧的代价》，但它既带有一种隐含的神秘主义维度，也同样蕴含着存在主义色彩。让人回想起1972年《金谷》（迷云）等嬉皮士时代的寻根电影，《西拉特》——这部注定要在拥有顶级音响系统的大银幕上观看的电影——是一场名副其实的迷幻之旅，只是比他们当年制作的任何作品都要喧嚣、更具爆发力。——乔纳森·罗姆尼（Jonathan Romney）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这一切看起来是如此典型的柯南伯格风格：奇异的身体、推测性的科技、巴洛克式的阴谋、反常的病理现象。然而，《裹尸布》——这位大师最具有欺骗性、最难以捉摸的作品之一——的核心关切，恰恰正是“表象”的问题。影片从潜意识开始，以一个将我们所见一切化为纯粹幻象的场景结束，它不是一部关于身体的电影，而是一部关于心灵的电影，它执着地向观众传达着自身作为影像的地位。这些科技惊悚片的行头更像是一种症状而非情节；它们逐渐陷入自相矛盾和毫无意义的过程，本身就是影片的重点所在。今年有很多电影都在探讨我们当下的生活方式，但唯独《裹尸布》精准捕捉到了我们自由坠入无尽内容旋涡中的状态、我们对奇观的迷恋所付出的代价，以及一个无法理解“媒介即讯息”的文化的政治谵妄。——内森·李（Nathan Lee）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "玛丽·布龙斯坦（Mary Bronstein）的第二部剧情长片是一个关于母亲的故事。女儿虽然处于这场压力风暴的核心，但在整部电影中始终未曾露面；用布龙斯坦的话说，她的故事应当由她自己来讲述。但对于我这个身为某个母亲的女儿、却从未做过任何人母亲的观众而言，《如果我有腿我一定踢你》展开时，却带着一种感同身受的痛苦与自传般的浓烈强度。这是一部危机接踵而至的电影，它唤起了我曾经身处前排、亲眼目睹我自己的母亲经历那种专属母亲的“冒名顶替综合征”的回忆。我并没有饮食失调，我的父亲也不是一个常年不在家的船长，我们的天花板也没有轰然坍塌。然而，罗斯·伯恩（Rose Byrne）脸上的那种表情——绝望地在内疚、恐惧、愤怒和爱之间挣扎——是我曾经见过的，如今又带着极大的同理心被唤醒。这要归功于布龙斯坦和她非凡的演员阵容（包括反差出演心理医生的柯南·奥布莱恩），让这样一部情绪幅度极大、有时甚至显得异想天开——既令人捧腹又让人神经紧绷——的电影，感觉如此真实贴近生活。——黛维卡·吉里什（Devika Girish）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "雅各布·库格勒（Ryan Coogler）此前已经执导过《洛奇》（Rocky）和《黑豹》（Black Panther），显然是一位雄心勃勃、而且极其成功的神话缔造者。大银幕上可曾呈现过如库格勒的《罪人》（Sinners）这般强劲融合黑人音乐、黑人宗教与黑人解放的作品？仅凭那段疯狂的、反向的Afrofuturist（非裔未来主义）舞蹈片段，就足以让这部电影成为我今年看过的第二强硬的电影大片（仅次于《一个接一个》）——它的重头戏虽然集中在前部，但其神采飞扬的劲头，几乎让人可以原谅罗伯特·罗德里格斯（Robert Rodriguez）式那种令人厌烦且过时的结局。特罗尔（Terroir）超越了密西西比三角洲的恐怖：库格勒不仅吸收了电影艺术家阿瑟·杰法（Arthur Jafa）关于神圣与世俗的理念，还吸收了他对场所的感知，将电影背景设定在克拉克斯代尔（Clarksdale）——这里是天才萨姆·库克（Sam Cooke）、约翰·李·胡克（John Lee Hooker）、孙·豪斯（Son House）、罗伯特·约翰逊（Robert Johnson）、伊克·特纳（Ike Turner）、穆迪·沃特斯（Muddy Waters）以及田纳西·威廉斯（Tennessee Williams）的故乡。杰法也是在那里长大的。我很想听听他对这部电影的看法。——J·霍伯曼（J. Hoberman）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "葡萄牙电影大师米格尔·戈麦斯（Miguel Gomes）的第六部长片由他和妻子兼长期合作者莫琳·法赞代罗（Maureen Fazendeiro）共同编剧，是一部兼具忧郁与充沛人文主义气息、极具电影感和浪漫色彩的复合之作。《壮游》（Grand Tour）将两位主角之间的情感距离具象化：爱德华（Gonçalo Waddington饰）是英国的一名年轻外交使节，焦虑地盘算着他在第一次世界大战时期的东亚即将到来的婚姻；而莫莉（Crista Alfaiate饰）则是一位性格开朗、心胸豁达的未婚妻，她千里迢迢赶来，在缅甸的驻地与未婚夫团聚，却发现他已经消失得无影无踪，而坚强且随性的她不得不踏上追寻他的足迹，开启了一条漫无计划的跨洲逃避路线。戈麦斯与其摄影师团队那躁动不安的摄影机，在特定历史背景下的剧本场景（在意大利搭建的摄影棚布景中拍摄）与相应现实地点的纪录片素材之间灵巧地交替：这是一场强有力的故事、主体、景观和声音的叠加，交织出了一部万花筒般的、游历四方的幻想曲。——玛德琳·惠特尔（Madeline Whittle）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "伊拉·萨克斯（Ira Sachs）这部极具电影感的作品，通过重现作家琳达·罗森克兰茨（Linda Rosenkrantz）与摄影师彼得·胡贾尔（Peter Hujar）之间磁带录音的对话，堪称一堂关于冗余创作可能性的生动课。当胡贾尔以极度严谨的细节回忆他在纽约市生活中的某一天时——这是一场平凡与非凡之间迷人的交融，让人想起《安迪·沃霍尔的哲学》——我们的焦点从他言说的主题，转向了记忆转化为素材的过程。本·威士肖（Ben Whishaw）对胡贾尔的出色演绎取材自对话的文字记录（而非现已丢失的罗森克兰茨原始录音），展现了所有演员工作背后的富有想象力的翻译任务。尽管萨克斯的电影有着令人激动的冗长，但它是一首对倾听艺术的赞歌，是对那种在其中“值得纪念”与“平凡琐碎”之间的等级不复存在的亲密友情空间的致敬。——斯里坎特·斯里尼瓦桑（Srikanth Srinivasan）", "translated": true}, "根据可以追溯到至少笛卡尔时期的某种哲学思想，根本没有“好习惯”这种东西——那些未经思考的重复动作会背叛一个人的自我控制感。露丝（凯瑟琳·查尔方特饰）是萨拉·弗里德兰这部不带一丝矫揉造作的温柔长片处女作中骄傲且有原则的八旬主角，她肯定会同意这一点。作为一名退休厨师，她习惯了将自己的意志施加于世界，但痴呆症开始模糊她与环境之间的界限。因此，她必须适应新的环境——一家高档但冷清的辅助生活设施那温暖的灯光和大地色调。穿透外部过渡的种种紧张，弗里德兰的电影以谦逊和细致描绘了内心的转变。露丝不再是自己思想和行为的主宰，她那根深蒂固的习惯与仪式——触摸、进食、烹饪的方式——作为身体的痕迹浮现出来，解锁了潜藏的记忆与被遗忘的联系。这部电影以100 percent的诚意，对心智与身体提供了安静、敏锐观察所得的洞见——杰森·福克斯", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "每隔一段时间，总会有这样一个时刻：一个怀疑论者再也无法否认眼前的证据，不得不成为一个真正的信徒，哪怕只是短暂地。《在溪边》（By the Stream）就是这样一部细腻而美妙的电影，它对本人——此前从未真正对洪常秀的狂热买账的人——产生了这样的效果。一个关于校园戏剧、长辈般的爱意以及颠覆性浪漫的故事，在充满温柔忧郁的秋日基调中徐徐展开，由洪常秀的御用演员金敏喜和权海骁的出色表演作为支撑。在充斥着各种电影极客大肆吹嘘的一年里，《在溪边》及时地提醒了我们：在合适的人手中，微小如何能够孕育出宏大。——埃里卡·巴尔索姆（Erika Mohawk）中大致扮演了此人）命名的村庄出发——来到奥马哈的一起林奇事件，少年方达曾刻骨铭心地目睹了这一幕（这在银幕上的《 ox-bow incident 》中得到了回响），再到福特的《侠骨柔情》（My Darling Clementine）中那个现代的图姆斯通，在那里，扭曲的历史每天都在为了旅游业而被重新演绎。也许这里最刻意唤起的方达电影并不是亨利的某部作品，而是他的儿子彼得·方达的《逍遥骑士》（Easy Rider）：这是一次穿越美国心脏地带的奥德赛之旅，挑战了我们的基本假设。——史蒂芬·米尔斯（Steven Mears）", "translated": true}, {"type": "我从未想过，一部通常充斥着老套路、艺术家的传记片，能如此优雅地重现洛伦茨·哈特歌词中那种机智与忧郁交织的鸡尾酒风味。理查德·林克莱特的电影将我们安顿在萨迪餐厅舒适且带着酒香的避难所里，那是1943年百老汇首演“俄克拉荷马惊叹号”的当晚，正如哈特尖酸刻薄地将他的昔日创意搭档理查德·罗杰斯与奥斯卡·汉默斯坦二世的新合作称作的那样——他深知这将是一部轰动之作，并预示着他自己那种都市、苦乐参半的歌曲风格将走向末日。伊桑·霍克奇迹般地赋予了哈特那种迷人、无可遏制的聪慧以及令人心碎的自我欺骗以生命力。罗伯特·卡普洛这部如同滑稽情人节般的剧本并没有浪费时间去对一个自我毁灭的天才进行心理分析，而是让我们在一旁偷听他阐述内韵与遣词造句的艺术，并参与一场接一场的妙语连珠与对唱马拉松——我最喜欢的是他与语气讽刺、轻声细语的同道中人E·B·怀特（帕特里克·肯尼迪饰）的对话。我走出剧院时，嘴里哼着台词，心中怀揣着一曲高歌——伊莫根·萨拉·史密斯", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本·罗素和纪尧姆·卡约这部时长三个半小时的纪录片片名带着一种狡黠的讽刺。听起来像是一部充满手持晃动镜头、抗议色情意味的激进宣传片的作品，实际上却对主题采取了更为克制的手法，捕捉了法国大西洋海岸附近ZAD（意为“保卫区”）集体成员的日常生活。这个无政府主义社团过去几十年一直在成功抵抗——通过路障、破坏以及现在被国家贴上“生态恐怖主义”标签的其他活动——法国政府为修建机场而进行的清地。但正是公社里的日常起居——烤面包、打铁、务农、办孩子的生日派对——在影片史诗般的人片时长中吸引了卡约和罗素的注意，全片仅由约40个构图严谨的镜头组成。当我们到达高潮段落时，数万名抗议者与数百名气势汹汹的警察发生冲突，这些微小的行为已汇聚成一个深度参与的生存与关怀项目，与该团体的激进主义同样重要，在法西斯主义抬头的时代勾勒出了一套全面的抵抗精神——里奥·戈德史密斯", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "玛莎·希林斯基这部戛纳评审团奖得主作品在女孩与女性多个时代的磨难中穿针引线，编织出一条蜿蜒的道路，构建成一幅跨代创伤的发烧般愿景。同一个乡村东德背景在1910年代和1940年代是一个家族庄园，在1980年代是一个村庄，在当下则是一处度假屋，每一处都以精妙的细节得以实现。从一个青春期女孩——一名农场长工——凝视着截肢者汗水淋漓的躯干这一开场画面开始，希林斯基从战争、家庭和父权虐待的悲剧中唤起了一种萦绕不去的抒情主义。控制、渴望和抛弃的力量弥漫在这些事件中，为影片注入了黑暗的感官色彩，使得河中游泳或捉迷藏这类田园插曲变成了生存的暗门。影片大师级的剪辑将这些截然不同的时刻串联成跨越时间的更大一系列联想纽带，赋予了其主角们一场共同的逃亡——凯文·B·李", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "鲁加诺·尼奥尼的反传统黑色喜剧《成为几内亚比绍母鸡》以主人公舒拉（苏珊·查迪饰）——一位年轻的赞比亚女性——在一条空旷的土路旁发现其叔叔弗德的尸体拉开帷幕。她当时正从一个化装舞会开车回家，打扮成音乐录影带《雨》中的米西·埃利奥特，穿着膨胀的黑色西装，戴着镶有珠宝的安全帽。她那冷若冰霜的平静与面无表情——从她发现弗德的尸体，到充满戏剧性的赞比亚哀悼仪式和葬礼筹备——揭示了一个令人不安、未曾言说却在不断溃烂的代际创伤。我们了解到，弗德不仅是一名连环强奸犯，而且家族中的年长女性还自封为他的保护者，守护着这个黑暗的秘密。在处女作2017年的《我不是女巫》所展现的女性主义觉醒基础上，尼奥尼对阿姨们和侄女们在尊重长辈与拉响父权暴力警报之间小心翼翼走钢丝时产生的冲突，提供了一幅既亲密又熟悉的肖像——马泰内·图雷", "translated": true}]

After its bombastic prologue, Paul Thomas Anderson’s typically sprawling tale skips 16 years ahead to follow befuddled ex-revolutionary Bob Ferguson (Leonardo DiCaprio), now living in hiding with his biracial teenage daughter, Willa (Chase Infiniti, incandescent). Then the white supremacist Col. Lockjaw (Sean Penn)—who, despite himself, has a thing for Black women, particularly Willa’s mom, Perfidia Beverly Hills (Teyana Taylor)—comes for the teenager. Bob is forced back into his previous life, chasing her down with help from former comrades and Willa’s karate instructor, Sergio (Benicio Del Toro, fully committed). The film’s paranoia-driven, pulsating action sequences illustrate not ideology but rather the infrastructure of allegiance—the signals, lingo, plans, and solidarity that sustain any embattled collective. Willa, after witnessing all the double-crossing, doubt, and sacrifice, still chooses to join the cause—now that’s a message worth salvaging.— Abby Sun"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cinema is full of hapless would-be criminals whose best-laid plans go awry, but the heist planned by J.B. Mooney (Josh O’Connor) in Kelly Reichardt’s The Mastermind is one of the worst-laid plans ever. Mooney is a master only in his own mind, having exhausted his one asset—charm—without realizing it. His neglected wife (Alana Haim) and two children, his retired-judge father (Bill Camp), and his club-lady mother (Hope Davis) have all indulged him, but his time is running out. Significantly, the film is set in the ’70s, a period of social activism (J.B.’s not interested) when it was easier not to grow up. At one point he calls his wife to say that all he’s done has been for the family—or, well, “three-quarters of it.” To say it’s anti-genre is not enough; it’s a wildly original take on a type rarely seen on screen because the interest here is in absence rather than presence. The Mastermind is a comic-horror story of a man who’s an utter vacuum, incapable of self-knowledge or change.— Molly Haskell"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Leave it to Kleber Mendonça Filho, a filmmaker for whom cinema feels as essential as breathing, to craft a political thriller that is equally steeped in the techniques of its classic-movie inspirations and the everyday atmospheres and textures of 1970s Brazil. Photographed in widescreen Panavision, and featuring De Palma–style split-diopter shots, Altmanesque zooms, and wipe transitions straight out of Star Wars , The Secret Agent is packed with period-perfect details and held together by Wagner Moura’s soulful performance as a scientist and father caught in the murderous headlights of Brazil’s military dictatorship. But this is also a movie that keeps wandering around—“a bit improvised, Brazilian-style,” as one character says. Mendonça is fascinated by how the history and tools of cinema become an archive; the film finds its most arresting images and moral conscience in all the supposedly unnecessary, extra stuff of life that one might imagine any other filmmaker excising from the record.— Michael Blair"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "In Jafar Panahi’s latest, a car mechanic, Vahid (Vahid Mobasseri), struggles with whether to kill the man whom he is almost certain tortured him in prison. Vahid is not a prince, but his dilemma—and Panahi’s road movie—reminded me of Hamlet , specifically “The Mousetrap,” the play that Hamlet commissions to prove that his uncle is guilty of murder. “Comical-tragical” is the desired effect of “The Mousetrap,” and it is a perfect genre designation for It Was Just an Accident and its central image—a truck holding a semiconscious man in a coffin-like box in the back, which Vahid drives around Tehran, picking up passengers who might help him decide whether killing a killer will change his life or the country they still love. Shot without permits barely a year after Panahi was released from his second prison term, the film was a risk that he and his team agreed to take; you can feel their will to speak truth to power in every second. No surprise, the much-deserved acclaim has also earned Panahi an in-absentia prison sentence.— Amy Taubin"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "What is there to hold on to in a changing world? Caught by the Tides leaves this question open. The film takes place during China’s early-21st-century economic transformation, long the subject of Jia Zhangke’s career. Here his attention turns inward: he reuses footage from his earlier films to construct the sweeping story of the fractured romance between Qiaoqiao (Zhao Tao) and Bin (Li Zhubin). Radio broadcasts index historic moments, like when China wins its bid to host the 2008 Olympics. But heaven is high and the emperor is far away: Jia is more concerned with what happens on the ever-shifting ground, the propulsive movements of people, and especially the expressions that flit across Zhao’s face. In the final third of the film, she wears a mask that covers all but her eyes. But what eyes they are—yearning and searching, they take in the broken man that Bin has become, a man as restless as his country.— Genevieve Yue"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Peruvian torero Andrés Roca Rey, his face contorted into a Harpo Marx–worthy grimace, stares down a slack-jawed, stumbling, rapidly dying bull. Decked out in the traditional gilded uniform (a traje de luces , or “suit of lights”), smeared with blood and the dust of the arena floor, the man arches his back and puffs out his chest, a posture of masculinity so exaggerated as to become abstract. In Afternoons of Solitude , Albert Serra’s first feature documentary, the roving, probing camera shows us that these rituals are simply the scaffolding, devoid of meaning in themselves, upon which the bullfighter hangs his days. Serra searches Roca Rey’s face in vain for a glimmer of self-awareness or acknowledgement that his life is essentially that of an animal trotted out to perform a play based on medieval ideas of honor. The line between man and beast, the film suggests, is as flimsy as the ripped white spandex, soaked in both human and bull’s blood, that Roca Rey tears off after another grimly successful corrida.— Clinton Krute"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "There’s no actual sex in Alain Guiraudie’s puckish policier, but the power of desire courses through the film’s lifeblood to uniquely sly and suspenseful ends. Following a handsome drifter (Félix Kysyl) upon his return to his rural hometown, the film unfolds a wily network of subterranean urges as the people around him—folks of all ages, genders, and professions—are drawn into his orbit, prompting enigmatic encounters that range from tender to murderous. Misericordia ’s provincial setting (Guiraudie’s native region of Occitania, in southern France), ambient sensuality, and shame-laced unease offer variations on the director’s enduring themes. Yet the film also stands out in his body of work for its masterful mélange of moods and genres, shifting between farce and philosophy with the elegant fickleness of autumn leaves tossing in the breeze.— Beatrice Loayza"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The Galician director of 2019’s Fire Will Come returns to Morocco, the location of his mystically charged Mimosas (2016). Like that film, Sirāt is a road movie about the place where the roads run out and the desert—and unpredictable destiny—takes over. Sergi López stars as a man searching for his daughter, joining forces with an alternative family of seasoned rave veterans (played by a troupe of grittily authentic nonprofessionals). With its bold narrative shock tactics and pounding techno score, Laxe’s latest comes across as a 21st-century Wages of Fear , but with an implicit spiritual dimension as much as an existential one. Harking back to hippie-era quest movies like 1972’s The Valley (Obscured by Clouds) , Sirāt —which demands to be seen on a big screen, with a sound system to match—is the proverbial trip, but louder and more explosive than any they made back then.— Jonathan Romney"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "It all appears so eminently Cronenbergian: weird bodies, speculative technologies, baroque conspiracies, aberrant pathologies. And yet the fundamental concern of The Shrouds —one of the master’s most deceptive, elusive works—is precisely the problem of appearance. Opening in the unconscious and closing with a scene that turns everything we’ve seen into pure phantasm, this is a movie not of the body but of the mind, a film that insistently telegraphs its own status as image. The techno-thriller trappings constitute a symptom rather than a plot; their progressive collapse into contradiction and pointlessness is very much the point. A lot of movies this year fussed over The Way We Live Now, but it was The Shrouds that nailed our free fall into a vortex of endless content, the toll inflicted by our attachment to spectacle, and the political delirium of a culture that fails to grasp how the medium is the message.— Nathan Lee"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Mary Bronstein’s second feature is a mother’s tale. The daughter, though at the crux of this stresscapade, remains off screen throughout; her story is hers to tell, as Bronstein has said. But for this viewer, the daughter of a mother and not the mother of anyone, If I Had Legs I’d Kick You unfolded with the gut-wrenching intensity of autobiography. A movie of cascading crises, it conjured memories of witnessing, with front-row access, my own amma undergoing the impostor syndrome so specific to mothers. I did not have a feeding disorder, my father was not a mostly absent boat captain, and our ceiling didn’t come crashing down. Yet the look on Rose Byrne’s face, as it desperately straddles guilt, fear, anger, and love, is one I’ve seen, and now recall with great empathy. It’s a credit to Bronstein and her extraordinary cast (including Conan O’Brien as a therapist, playing against type) that a movie of such huge, sometimes outlandish swings—as laugh-inducing as they are nerve-wracking—feels so true to life.— Devika Girish"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Having already tackled Rocky and the Black Panther, Ryan Coogler is clearly an ambitious, not to mention mega-successful, mythmaker. Has the big screen ever advanced as potent a mix of Black music, Black religion, and Black liberation as Coogler’s Sinners ? The mad, Afrofuturist-in-reverse dance sequence alone would make this the second-strongest movie -movie I saw this year (next to One Battle After Another )—it’s frontloaded for sure, but with so much brio that one can almost forgive the tediously passé Robert Rodriguez–esque finale. Terroir transcends terror in the Mississippi Delta: Coogler has absorbed not only film artist Arthur Jafa’s ideas regarding the sacred and the profane, but his sense of place, too, having set the movie in Clarksdale—hometown of geniuses Sam Cooke, John Lee Hooker, Son House, Robert Johnson, Ike Turner, Muddy Waters, and Tennessee Williams. Jafa grew up there as well. I’d love to get his take on the movie.— J. Hoberman"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "The sixth feature from Portuguese auteur Miguel Gomes, co-written with his wife and frequent collaborator Maureen Fazendeiro, is a thrillingly cinematic and romantic concoction of melancholy and effervescent humanism. Grand Tour literalizes the emotional distance separating its two protagonists: Edward (Gonçalo Waddington), a young diplomatic envoy of the British Empire anxiously contemplating his impending marriage in World War I–era East Asia; and Molly (Crista Alfaiate), the irrepressibly openhearted fiancée who arrives to join her betrothed where he’s stationed in Burma—only to find him vanished, and herself, intrepid and indulgent, obliged to follow in his wake as he charts a haphazard cross-continental route of evasion. Gomes and his cinematographers’ restless camera alternates nimbly between period-set scripted scenes (filmed in Italy on constructed soundstage sets) and documentary footage of the corresponding real-world locations: a potent layering of stories, subjects, sights, and sounds that together yield a kaleidoscopic and peripatetic fantasia.— Madeline Whittle"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Ira Sachs’s eminently cinematic re-creation of a tape-recorded conversation between writer Linda Rosenkrantz (Rebecca Hall) and photographer Peter Hujar (Ben Whishaw) is an object lesson in the creative possibilities of redundancy. As Hujar recollects a day from his life in New York City in rigorous detail—a fascinating mix of the ordinary and the extraordinary, recalling The Philosophy of Andy Warhol —our focus turns from the content of his speech to the process by which memory becomes material. Drawing from transcripts of the conversation—and not Rosenkrantz’s original recording, now lost—Whishaw’s incredibly textured performance as Hujar reveals the task of imaginative translation that underlies all actorly work. For all its thrilling verbosity, Sachs’s film is a tribute to the art of listening, to this intimate space of friendship in which the hierarchy between the memorable and the mundane ceases to exist.— Srikanth Srinivasan"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "According to a line of philosophical thought dating back to at least Descartes, there are no such things as good habits—those unthinking repetitions that betray one’s sense of self-control. Ruth (Kathleen Chalfant), the proud and principled octogenarian protagonist of Sarah Friedland’s tender-without-an-ounce-of-the-mawkish feature debut, would surely agree. A retired cook, she’s accustomed to exercising her will upon the world, but dementia is starting to scramble the boundaries between herself and her environment. So she must habituate to new surroundings—to the warm lighting and earth tones of an upscale but sterile assisted-living facility. Through the strains of this external transition, Friedland’s film pictures an internal one with humility and care. Ruth is no longer a master of her thoughts and actions, and her ingrained habits and rituals—ways of touching, eating, cooking—emerge as physical traces that unlock latent memories and forgotten connections. This is a film that offers quiet, sharply observed insights about the mind and body with 100 percent heart.— Jason Fox"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Every so often it happens that a skeptic can no longer deny the evidence in front of her and must become a true believer, even if only temporarily. article_text:
The results are now in for our 2025 poll of Film Comment ’s contributors! On this page, you’ll find our list of the 20 best films that were released either theatrically or virtually in 2025 in the United States, with original appreciations from our critics, as well as links to features, reviews, and interviews about these films and directors from throughout the year.

Also check out our list of the Best Undistributed Films of 2025. Our voters’ Individual Ballots , and our Best of 2025 Countdown Podcast , featuring guest critics Amy Taubin and Bilge Ebiri, will be online tomorrow. Coming next week: critic and programmer Inney Prakash’s list of the year’s Best Short Films , filmmaker and programmer Gina Telaroli’s list of the Best Restorations , critic and editor Gavin Smith’s list of the year’s Best Repertory Releases, and writing on the Best Scenes by Devika Girish and the Best Performances by Michael Koresky.

Subscribe today to the Film Comment Letter—the best way to stay on top of all our Best of 2025 coverage.

Those claiming that One Battle After Another reduces its characters to caricature misread what the film anatomizes: the mechanics of loyalty. After its bombastic prologue, Paul Thomas Anderson’s typically sprawling tale skips 16 years ahead to follow befuddled ex-revolutionary Bob Ferguson (Leonardo DiCaprio), now living in hiding with his biracial teenage daughter, Willa (Chase Infiniti, incandescent). Then the white supremacist Col. Lockjaw (Sean Penn)—who, despite himself, has a thing for Black women, particularly Willa’s mom, Perfidia Beverly Hills (Teyana Taylor)—comes for the teenager. Bob is forced back into his previous life, chasing her down with help from former comrades and Willa’s karate instructor, Sergio (Benicio Del Toro, fully committed). The film’s paranoia-driven, pulsating action sequences illustrate not ideology but rather the infrastructure of allegiance—the signals, lingo, plans, and solidarity that sustain any embattled collective. Willa, after witnessing all the double-crossing, doubt, and sacrifice, still chooses to join the cause—now that’s a message worth salvaging.— Abby Sun

Cinema is full of hapless would-be criminals whose best-laid plans go awry, but the heist planned by J.B. Mooney (Josh O’Connor) in Kelly Reichardt’s The Mastermind is one of the worst-laid plans ever. Mooney is a master only in his own mind, having exhausted his one asset—charm—without realizing it. His neglected wife (Alana Haim) and two children, his retired-judge father (Bill Camp), and his club-lady mother (Hope Davis) have all indulged him, but his time is running out. Significantly, the film is set in the ’70s, a period of social activism (J.B.’s not interested) when it was easier not to grow up. At one point he calls his wife to say that all he’s done has been for the family—or, well, “three-quarters of it.” To say it’s anti-genre is not enough; it’s a wildly original take on a type rarely seen on screen because the interest here is in absence rather than presence. The Mastermind is a comic-horror story of a man who’s an utter vacuum, incapable of self-knowledge or change.— Molly Haskell

Leave it to Kleber Mendonça Filho, a filmmaker for whom cinema feels as essential as breathing, to craft a political thriller that is equally steeped in the techniques of its classic-movie inspirations and the everyday atmospheres and textures of 1970s Brazil. Photographed in widescreen Panavision, and featuring De Palma–style split-diopter shots, Altmanesque zooms, and wipe transitions straight out of Star Wars , The Secret Agent is packed with period-perfect details and held together by Wagner Moura’s soulful performance as a scientist and father caught in the murderous headlights of Brazil’s military dictatorship. But this is also a movie that keeps wandering around—“a bit improvised, Brazilian-style,” as one character says. Mendonça is fascinated by how the history and tools of cinema become an archive; the film finds its most arresting images and moral conscience in all the supposedly unnecessary, extra stuff of life that one might imagine any other filmmaker excising from the record.— Michael Blair

In Jafar Panahi’s latest, a car mechanic, Vahid (Vahid Mobasseri), struggles with whether to kill the man whom he is almost certain tortured him in prison. Vahid is not a prince, but his dilemma—and Panahi’s road movie—reminded me of Hamlet , specifically “The Mousetrap,” the play that Hamlet commissions to prove that his uncle is guilty of murder. “Comical-tragical” is the desired effect of “The Mousetrap,” and it is a perfect genre designation for It Was Just an Accident and its central image—a truck holding a semiconscious man in a coffin-like box in the back, which Vahid drives around Tehran, picking up passengers who might help him decide whether killing a killer will change his life or the country they still love. Shot without permits barely a year after Panahi was released from his second prison term, the film was a risk that he and his team agreed to take; you can feel their will to speak truth to power in every second. No surprise, the much-deserved acclaim has also earned Panahi an in-absentia prison sentence.— Amy Taubin

What is there to hold on to in a changing world? Caught by the Tides leaves this question open. The film takes place during China’s early-21st-century economic transformation, long the subject of Jia Zhangke’s career. Here his attention turns inward: he reuses footage from his earlier films to construct the sweeping story of the fractured romance between Qiaoqiao (Zhao Tao) and Bin (Li Zhubin). Radio broadcasts index historic moments, like when China wins its bid to host the 2008 Olympics. But heaven is high and the emperor is far away: Jia is more concerned with what happens on the ever-shifting ground, the propulsive movements of people, and especially the expressions that flit across Zhao’s face. In the final third of the film, she wears a mask that covers all but her eyes. But what eyes they are—yearning and searching, they take in the broken man that Bin has become, a man as restless as his country.— Genevieve Yue

The Peruvian torero Andrés Roca Rey, his face contorted into a Harpo Marx–worthy grimace, stares down a slack-jawed, stumbling, rapidly dying bull. Decked out in the traditional gilded uniform (a traje de luces , or “suit of lights”), smeared with blood and the dust of the arena floor, the man arches his back and puffs out his chest, a posture of masculinity so exaggerated as to become abstract. In Afternoons of Solitude , Albert Serra’s first feature documentary, the roving, probing camera shows us that these rituals are simply the scaffolding, devoid of meaning in themselves, upon which the bullfighter hangs his days. Serra searches Roca Rey’s face in vain for a glimmer of self-awareness or acknowledgement that his life is essentially that of an animal trotted out to perform a play based on medieval ideas of honor. The line between man and beast, the film suggests, is as flimsy as the ripped white spandex, soaked in both human and bull’s blood, that Roca Rey tears off after another grimly successful corrida.— Clinton Krute

There’s no actual sex in Alain Guiraudie’s puckish policier, but the power of desire courses through the film’s lifeblood to uniquely sly and suspenseful ends. Following a handsome drifter (Félix Kysyl) upon his return to his rural hometown, the film unfolds a wily network of subterranean urges as the people around him—folks of all ages, genders, and professions—are drawn into his orbit, prompting enigmatic encounters that range from tender to murderous. Misericordia ’s provincial setting (Guiraudie’s native region of Occitania, in southern France), ambient sensuality, and shame-laced unease offer variations on the director’s enduring themes. Yet the film also stands out in his body of work for its masterful mélange of moods and genres, shifting between farce and philosophy with the elegant fickleness of autumn leaves tossing in the breeze.— Beatrice Loayza

The Galician director of 2019’s Fire Will Come returns to Morocco, the location of his mystically charged Mimosas (2016). Like that film, Sirāt is a road movie about the place where the roads run out and the desert—and unpredictable destiny—takes over. Sergi López stars as a man searching for his daughter, joining forces with an alternative family of seasoned rave veterans (played by a troupe of grittily authentic nonprofessionals). With its bold narrative shock tactics and pounding techno score, Laxe’s latest comes across as a 21st-century Wages of Fear , but with an implicit spiritual dimension as much as an existential one. Harking back to hippie-era quest movies like 1972’s The Valley (Obscured by Clouds) , Sirāt —which demands to be seen on a big screen, with a sound system to match—is the proverbial trip, but louder and more explosive than any they made back then.— Jonathan Romney

It all appears so eminently Cronenbergian: weird bodies, speculative technologies, baroque conspiracies, aberrant pathologies. And yet the fundamental concern of The Shrouds —one of the master’s most deceptive, elusive works—is precisely the problem of appearance. Opening in the unconscious and closing with a scene that turns everything we’ve seen into pure phantasm, this is a movie not of the body but of the mind, a film that insistently telegraphs its own status as image. The techno-thriller trappings constitute a symptom rather than a plot; their progressive collapse into contradiction and pointlessness is very much the point. A lot of movies this year fussed over The Way We Live Now, but it was The Shrouds that nailed our free fall into a vortex of endless content, the toll inflicted by our attachment to spectacle, and the political delirium of a culture that fails to grasp how the medium is the message.— Nathan Lee

Mary Bronstein’s second feature is a mother’s tale. The daughter, though at the crux of this stresscapade, remains off screen throughout; her story is hers to tell, as Bronstein has said. But for this viewer, the daughter of a mother and not the mother of anyone, If I Had Legs I’d Kick You unfolded with the gut-wrenching intensity of autobiography. A movie of cascading crises, it conjured memories of witnessing, with front-row access, my own amma undergoing the impostor syndrome so specific to mothers. I did not have a feeding disorder, my father was not a mostly absent boat captain, and our ceiling didn’t come crashing down. Yet the look on Rose Byrne’s face, as it desperately straddles guilt, fear, anger, and love, is one I’ve seen, and now recall with great empathy. It’s a credit to Bronstein and her extraordinary cast (including Conan O’Brien as a therapist, playing against type) that a movie of such huge, sometimes outlandish swings—as laugh-inducing as they are nerve-wracking—feels so true to life.— Devika Girish

Having already tackled Rocky and the Black Panther, Ryan Coogler is clearly an ambitious, not to mention mega-successful, mythmaker. Has the big screen ever advanced as potent a mix of Black music, Black religion, and Black liberation as Coogler’s Sinners ? The mad, Afrofuturist-in-reverse dance sequence alone would make this the second-strongest movie -movie I saw this year (next to One Battle After Another )—it’s frontloaded for sure, but with so much brio that one can almost forgive the tediously passé Robert Rodriguez–esque finale. Terroir transcends terror in the Mississippi Delta: Coogler has absorbed not only film artist Arthur Jafa’s ideas regarding the sacred and the profane, but his sense of place, too, having set the movie in Clarksdale—hometown of geniuses Sam Cooke, John Lee Hooker, Son House, Robert Johnson, Ike Turner, Muddy Waters, and Tennessee Williams. Jafa grew up there as well. I’d love to get his take on the movie.— J. Hoberman

The sixth feature from Portuguese auteur Miguel Gomes, co-written with his wife and frequent collaborator Maureen Fazendeiro, is a thrillingly cinematic and romantic concoction of melancholy and effervescent humanism. Grand Tour literalizes the emotional distance separating its two protagonists: Edward (Gonçalo Waddington), a young diplomatic envoy of the British Empire anxiously contemplating his impending marriage in World War I–era East Asia; and Molly (Crista Alfaiate), the irrepressibly openhearted fiancée who arrives to join her betrothed where he’s stationed in Burma—only to find him vanished, and herself, intrepid and indulgent, obliged to follow in his wake as he charts a haphazard cross-continental route of evasion. Gomes and his cinematographers’ restless camera alternates nimbly between period-set scripted scenes (filmed in Italy on constructed soundstage sets) and documentary footage of the corresponding real-world locations: a potent layering of stories, subjects, sights, and sounds that together yield a kaleidoscopic and peripatetic fantasia.— Madeline Whittle

Ira Sachs’s eminently cinematic re-creation of a tape-recorded conversation between writer Linda Rosenkrantz (Rebecca Hall) and photographer Peter Hujar (Ben Whishaw) is an object lesson in the creative possibilities of redundancy. As Hujar recollects a day from his life in New York City in rigorous detail—a fascinating mix of the ordinary and the extraordinary, recalling The Philosophy of Andy Warhol —our focus turns from the content of his speech to the process by which memory becomes material. Drawing from transcripts of the conversation—and not Rosenkrantz’s original recording, now lost—Whishaw’s incredibly textured performance as Hujar reveals the task of imaginative translation that underlies all actorly work. For all its thrilling verbosity, Sachs’s film is a tribute to the art of listening, to this intimate space of friendship in which the hierarchy between the memorable and the mundane ceases to exist.— Srikanth Srinivasan

According to a line of philosophical thought dating back to at least Descartes, there are no such things as good habits—those unthinking repetitions that betray one’s sense of self-control. Ruth (Kathleen Chalfant), the proud and principled octogenarian protagonist of Sarah Friedland’s tender-without-an-ounce-of-the-mawkish feature debut, would surely agree. A retired cook, she’s accustomed to exercising her will upon the world, but dementia is starting to scramble the boundaries between herself and her environment. So she must habituate to new surroundings—to the warm lighting and earth tones of an upscale but sterile assisted-living facility. Through the strains of this external transition, Friedland’s film pictures an internal one with humility and care. Ruth is no longer a master of her thoughts and actions, and her ingrained habits and rituals—ways of touching, eating, cooking—emerge as physical traces that unlock latent memories and forgotten connections. This is a film that offers quiet, sharply observed insights about the mind and body with 100 percent heart.— Jason Fox

Every so often it happens that a skeptic can no longer deny the evidence in front of her and must become a true believer, even if only temporarily. By the Stream is a film of such delicacy and delight that it had this effect on yours truly, someone who had never before quite bought into the Hong Sangsoo hype. A story of campus theater, avuncular affection, and disruptive romance unfolds in an autumn register full of gentle melancholy, anchored by wonderful performances from Hong regulars Kim Min-hee and Kwon Hae-hyo. In a year of so much film-bro bluster, By the Stream is a welcome reminder of how, in the right hands, smallness can give rise to grandeur.— Erika Balsom

When Henry Fonda scoffs at the idea that he personifies liberal American integrity, he’s performing the same “self-demystification” that critic, curator, and debuting filmmaker Alexander Horwath believes the U.S. is overdue for as a nation. The Austrian director’s method of peeling away the bromides of American exceptionalism is ingenious: he uses Fonda’s filmography and unsanitized family lore to document three centuries of social and political history. Never dull or didactic, Horwath shepherds us from the village of Fonda, New York, named for one of the actor’s colonial ancestors (whom he more or less played in John Ford’s mythologizing Drums Along the Mohawk ) to an Omaha lynching indelibly witnessed by a teenage Fonda (echoed on screen in The Ox-Bow Incident ), and to the present-day Tombstone of Ford’s My Darling Clementine , where distorted history is reenacted daily for the tourist trade. Perhaps the Fonda film most deliberately evoked here isn’t one of Henry’s, but his son Peter’s Easy Rider : an odyssey through the heart of America that contests our foundational assumptions.— Steven Mears

It never entered my mind that an artist biopic, a genre typically clogged with clichés, could so elegantly replicate the cocktail of wit and melancholy in Lorenz Hart’s lyrics. Richard Linklater’s film ensconces us in the cozy, boozy sanctuary of Sardi’s, on the night of the 1943 Broadway debut of “ Oklahoma exclamation point,” as Hart snidely refers to his erstwhile creative partner Richard Rodgers’s new collaboration with Oscar Hammerstein II—which he knows will be a smash hit, spelling doom for his own brand of urbane, bittersweet songs. Ethan Hawke miraculously animates Hart’s blend of charm, irrepressible cleverness, and heartbreaking self-delusion. Robert Kaplow’s funny valentine of a screenplay doesn’t waste time psychoanalyzing a self-destructive genius, instead letting us eavesdrop as he expounds on the art of interior rhymes and word choice, and engages in a marathon of verbal duels and duets—my favorite being his exchanges with the wry, soft-spoken kindred spirit E.B. White (Patrick Kennedy). I came out of the theater humming the dialogue, with a song in my heart.— Imogen Sara Smith

There’s a sly irony to the title of Ben Russell and Guillaume Cailleau’s three-and-a-half-hour documentary. What sounds like a work of shaky-cam, protest-porn agitprop takes, in fact, a more subdued approach to its subject, capturing the quotidian activities of the ZAD (in English, “Zone to Defend”) collective near France’s Atlantic coastline. This anarchist community has spent the past decades successfully fighting—via blockades, sabotage, and other activities now labeled “ecoterrorism” by the state—the clearance of land for the construction of an airport by the French government. But it’s the everyday life in the commune—baking, forging, farming, throwing a kid’s birthday party—that draws Cailleau and Russell’s attention across the film’s epic runtime, comprising only about 40 tightly composed shots. By the time we reach the climactic sequence, in which tens of thousands of protesters clash with hundreds of aggressive cops, these small acts have coalesced into a deeply engaged project of survival and care, as important as the group’s militancy, modeling a comprehensive ethos of resistance in an era of rising fascism.— Leo Goldsmith

Mascha Schilinski’s Cannes Jury Prize–winner weaves a sinuous path through the travails of multiple eras of girls and women, building into a feverish vision of cross-generational trauma. The same rural eastern German setting is incarnated as a family estate in the 1910s and 1940s, a village in the 1980s, and a vacation home in the present, each realized with exquisite detail. From the opening image of an adolescent girl—a farmhand—gazing at the sweat-beaded torso of an amputee, Schilinski conjures a haunted lyricism from tragedies of war, family, and patriarchal abuse. Forces of control, desire, and abandonment permeate these incidents and charge the film with a dark sensuality, such that pastoral interludes like a river swim or a game of hide-and-seek become existential trapdoors. The film’s magisterial editing links those disparate moments into a larger series of associative bonds across time, granting its protagonists a shared flight.— Kevin B. Lee

Rungano Nyoni’s offbeat black comedy On Becoming a Guinea Fowl opens with the protagonist, Shula (Susan Chardy), a young Zambian woman, discovering her Uncle Fred’s dead body by an empty dirt road. She’s driving home from a costume party dressed as Missy Elliot from the music video “The Rain,” in a ballooned black suit and a bejeweled helmet. Her deadpan demeanor and inexpressiveness—from the moment she finds Fred’s corpse through the theatrical Zambian mourning rituals and funeral preparations—reveal an unsettling generational wound that festers, unspoken. Not only was Fred a serial rapist, we learn, but the older women of the family have deputized themselves as his protectors, guarding this dark secret. Building on the feminist sensibilities of her debut feature, 2017’s I Am Not a Witch , Nyoni offers an intimate and familiar portrait of the clashes between the aunties and the nieces as they navigate a delicate line between respecting one’s elders and sounding the alarm on patriarchal violence.— Matene Toure

Coyote 从 Acme 买来各式各样的装置，想抓住 Papa-Léguas，却几乎总是沦为自家产品的受害者。如果你曾对这个小角色生出同情，大概也想过：那些不可靠产品引发的无数事故，公司难道不该负责吗？而《Coyote vs. Acme》恰恰就是因这个疑问而存在——它如此显而易见，同时又如此引人深思。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "导演 Dave Green 很擅长找到一种方式，既保留动画的精髓，又把角色放进不同的叙事结构里。又一次追逐以灾难收场后，筋疲力尽的 Coyote 考虑放弃自己不知疲倦的使命——此时，怀旧感笼罩了这场戏，往昔冒险的许多画面接连浮现。影片无需改变他的性格，甚至不必让他开口说话，就在他众所周知的固执里找到了脆弱。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Coyote 于是找到专攻缺陷产品的律师 Kevin Avery（Will Forte），要起诉 Acme。当他们意识到所面对的这家公司有多庞大——由 Buddy Crane（John Cena）代表——案件也随之升级。从这里开始，这部法庭喜剧吸纳了人类的官僚程序，却没有丢掉卡通逻辑。Green 并不试图把主角变得更写实，好让他融入这个环境。幽默来自要求现实世界以绝对的严肃态度对待动画的物理法则。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Will Forte 和 John Cena 起到对照作用，在需要以世俗的方式回应周围一切荒诞时表现良好。Avery 保持在普通律师的原型里，这从他与 Coyote 的相处中生出幽默。而 Buddy Crane 则是 Acme 自身傲慢的延伸，Cena 显然是这个漫画式角色的极佳人选。然而，当剧本离开动画角色、转去发展人类各自的冲突时，作品就失去了力量——那些纠葛太过琐碎，无法与那个卡通宇宙相抗衡。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其他 Looney Tunes 角色的出现帮助找回了能量，影片又没有变成一连串无谓的客串。他们的参与非常自然地融入故事，每当影片愿意深入动画与真人表演的混合，就能得分。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有趣的是，Acme 也不只是提供搞笑小玩意儿的供应商，还得到了进一步的发展。这家公司显露出对自己所售之物劣质的自觉，也强大到足以逃避责任。这种批评当然是轻巧的。但把 Coyote 与品牌的关系重新解释为某种商业依赖，自有其价值，尤其当长片揭示出公司的真实意图时。顺带一提，这也让影片在如此熟悉的套路里找到了新的一层。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管如此，为这部作品提供出人意料的情感重量的，正是 Coyote 本人。导演捕捉到了这种捕食者与猎物关系中的某种忧郁。Wile 从来没有真正抓住 Papa-Léguas 的可能，却仍然必须继续追下去——这个想法与片中神秘的“西西弗斯计划”相呼应。正是这种宿敌关系决定了两个角色的生活，也促成了一个出人意料地动情而温柔的结局。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Coyote vs. Acme》证明，不必重新发明 Looney Tunes 才能为新故事提供理由。老配方清晰可见，但怀旧只是起点，用来对角色做一次连贯而极具创意的更新。追了 Papa-Léguas 这么多年之后，要在 Coyote 身上找到新东西，最好的方式恰恰是理解他为什么永远停不下来。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Dave Green parte de décadas de absurdos dos Looney Tunes para fazer uma criativa comédia de tribunal sem descaracterizar seus personagens.

Já faz tempo que nos acostumamos ao eterno ciclo em que Wile E. Coyote compra toda espécie de engenhocas da Acme para tentar capturar o Papa-Léguas e quase sempre termina vítima do próprio produto. Se algum dia você sentiu empatia pelo personagem, já deve ter se perguntado se a empresa não deveria ser responsabilizada pelos inúmeros acidentes provocados pelos seus produtos pouco confiáveis. Pois bem, “ Coyote vs. Acme ” existe justamente por causa dessa dúvida, tão óbvia e, ao mesmo tempo, tão instigante.

O diretor Dave Green é muito competente ao encontrar uma maneira de preservar a essência dos desenhos enquanto coloca seus personagens dentro de uma estrutura narrativa diferente. Após mais uma perseguição terminar em desastre, o exausto Coyote considera abandonar sua incansável missão — nesse momento, a nostalgia toma conta da cena com várias imagens de aventuras anteriores aparecendo. Sem precisar alterar sua personalidade ou mesmo fazê-lo falar, o filme encontra vulnerabilidade na sua conhecida teimosia.

Coyote procura então Kevin Avery (Will Forte), advogado especializado em produtos defeituosos, para processar a Acme. O caso cresce quando os dois percebem o tamanho da empresa que estão enfrentando, representada por Buddy Crane (John Cena). A partir daí, a comédia de tribunal incorpora a burocracia dos humanos sem perder a lógica cartunesca. Green não tenta tornar o protagonista mais realista para encaixá-lo nesse ambiente. O humor vem de exigir que o mundo real trate a física dos desenhos com absoluta seriedade.

Will Forte e John Cena servem de contraponto, funcionando bem quando precisam reagir a todo o absurdo ao redor de forma mundana. Avery se mantém no arquétipo de um advogado comum, o que gera humor a partir da sua convivência com Coyote. Já Buddy Crane é uma extensão da arrogância da própria Acme, e Cena se mostra uma ótima escolha para o papel caricato. Contudo, quando o roteiro se afasta dos personagens animados para desenvolver os conflitos particulares dos humanos, a obra perde força — são dilemas triviais demais para competir com aquele universo cartunesco.

A presença de outros Looney Tunes ajuda a recuperar a energia sem que o filme se torne uma sequência de aparições gratuitas. Suas participações se integram à história com muita naturalidade, e o filme ganha pontos sempre que se dispõe a mergulhar na mistura entre animação e live-action.

É interessante ver que a Acme também ganha um desenvolvimento para além da fornecedora de bugigangas para piadas. A empresa se mostra consciente da precariedade do que vende e poderosa o suficiente para evitar responsabilidade. A crítica, obviamente, é leve. Mas reinterpretar a relação entre Coyote e a marca como uma espécie de dependência comercial tem seu mérito, principalmente quando o longa revela as verdadeiras intenções da corporação. De quebra, permite ao filme encontrar uma nova camada dentro de uma fórmula tão conhecida.

Apesar de tudo, quem fornece à produção seu inesperado peso emocional é o próprio Coyote. O diretor captura certa melancolia nessa relação entre predador e presa. Wile nunca teve uma possibilidade real de capturar o Papa-Léguas, mas ainda assim precisa continuar correndo atrás dele — uma ideia que se alinha ao misterioso Projeto Sísifo visto na obra. É essa rivalidade que dita a vida dos dois e permite um desfecho surpreendentemente emotivo e afetuoso.

“Coyote vs. Acme” é a prova de que não é preciso reinventar os Looney Tunes para justificar novas histórias. A velha fórmula está bem visível, mas a nostalgia serve apenas de ponto de partida para uma atualização coerente e muito criativa para os personagens. Depois de tantas décadas correndo atrás do Papa-Léguas, a melhor maneira de encontrar algo novo em Coyote era justamente entender por que ele nunca conseguia parar.

title_original: Rudi Fuchs, former director of Stedelijk Museum, 1942–2026
editorial_title_zh: 鲁迪·富克斯，市立博物馆前馆长，1942–2026
editorial_excerpt_zh: 这位策展人兼博物馆馆长以其独特的陈列方式而闻名

Croes / Anefo。图片鸣谢：荷兰国家档案馆，海牙", "credit": "ArtReview", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "鲁迪·富克斯（Rudi Fuchs）是一位具有影响力的策展人和博物馆馆长，于84岁高龄逝世。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "富克斯1942年出生于埃因霍温，曾在莱顿大学学习艺术史，并于1960年代末开始撰写关于艺术的文章。1975年，他成为埃因霍温凡·阿贝博物馆（Van Abbemuseum）馆长。在其任职期间，他显著扩充了该馆的欧洲现代与当代艺术收藏，并大力推崇乔治·巴泽利茨（Georg Baselitz）、扬·迪贝茨（Jan Dibbets）和丹尼尔·布伦（Daniel Buren）等艺术家，这一倾向贯穿了他的整个职业生涯。作为1982年第7届卡塞尔文献展的艺术总监，他阐明的主旨是彰显艺术的“尊严”。该展览侧重于绘画和雕塑，获得了褒贬不一的评价，一位评论家将其形容为“享乐宫殿”，而另一些人则批评富克斯采取了去政治化的方法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此后，富克斯继续其博物馆生涯，于1984年至1990年担任都灵里沃利城堡（Castello di Rivoli）艺术总监，1987年至1993年担任海牙市立博物馆（Gemeentemuseum）馆长，并于1993年至2003年担任阿姆斯特丹市立博物馆（Stedelijk Museum）馆长。在阿姆斯特丹市立博物馆，他以将不同艺术家和风格的作品结合在一起的独特陈列方式而闻名。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "2016年，富克斯作为客座策展人重返这家阿姆斯特丹机构，策划了回顾其自身职业生涯的展览《兴奋》（Excitement）。他在展览前言中总结自己的方法时写道：“1982年，当我的文献展以对话的形式呈现截然不同的作品时，《纽约时报》的评论家称我为‘浪漫主义法西斯’。但对我而言，这种组合充满力量且令人兴奋——这就是我这样做的原因——这样我和公众就能以全新的视角看待事物……一切都大不相同，这就是它为何行之有效的原因。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "分享", "links": [{"text": "Share", "url": "https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://artreview.com/rudi-fuchs-former-director-of-stedelijk-museum-1942-2026/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "list_item", "text": "推文", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Rudi Fuchs, an influential curator and museum director, has died age 84.

Born in Eindhoven in 1942, Fuchs studied art history at Leiden University and started writing about art in the late 1960s. In 1975, he became director of the Van Abbemuseum in Eindhoven. During his tenure, he significantly expanded the museum’s collection of European modern and contemporary art championing, among others, artists such as Georg Baselitz, Jan Dibbets and Daniel Buren, which he would continue to put forward throughout his career. As artistic director of Documenta 7 in 1982, his stated aim was to do justice to the ‘dignity’ of art. The exhibition, which was particularly heavy on paintings and sculptures, received mixed reviews, with one critic qualifying it as a ‘palace of pleasure’ and others criticising Fuchs’s apolitical approach.

Fuchs then continued his museum career, serving as artistic director of Castello di Rivoli in Turin from 1984 to 1990, director of the Gemeentemuseum in The Hague from 1987 to 1993 and director of the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam from 1993 to 2003. At the Stedelijk, he became known for his idiosyncratic displays that combined works from different artists and styles.

In 2016, Fuchs returned to the Amsterdam institution as guest curator for Excitement , an exhibition surveying his own career. In his exhibition text, summing up his approach, he wrote: ‘In 1982, when my Documenta presented very different works in a dialogue setting, the critic of the New York Times called me a “romantic fascist”. But to me, the combination was powerful and exciting – that’s why I did it – so that I, and the public, could see things from a fresh perspective… Everything’s very different, which is why it works.’

editorial_excerpt_zh: 继《le jeu》之后，ange 推出了单曲《pour te ramener à moi》，在其中孤独与派对交织。该音乐录影带目前正在所有 mk2 影院上映。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://www.troiscouleurs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/ANGE_PRESS_4-1-1024x576.jpg", "alt": "ANGE PRESS 4 1", "caption": "", "credit": "Trois Couleurs", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一个空房间、一块假天花板以及几乎带有礼拜仪式感的光晕……凭借《pour te ramener à moi》，这位所有歌曲都用小写字母书写的艺术家，为其计划于年底发行的 EP 的首支单曲倾注了宏大的手笔。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ange 与导演 Gaz 在音乐录影带的开篇呈现了一幅孤独的画面，这也预示着后续的发展。在这位艺术家周围（她的香烟总是夹在手指间），这个看起来像是空无一人的酒店逐渐挤满了受折磨的主角。人们很难不联想到斯坦利·库布里克（Stanley Kubrick）《闪灵》（Shining）中的全景酒店（Overlook Hotel）。在带有一丝怀旧色彩的歌词伴随下，一名男子在镜子前剃光了头，而另一名男子则狂热地起舞。一具躯体倒在地上，周围是五彩纸屑和狂欢。在录影带中，闭塞与解放交织摇摆。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "音乐同样承载着这些情感，游走于电子乐、流行乐和这位艺术家的说唱之间，该单曲由 BRUME(s) 制作，这是一个曾支持 Jolagreen 和 Roninia 等其他艺术家的厂牌。诞生于青少年卧室、汲取了集体说唱的密码，随后转向更具混合风格的音乐，ange 如今在 Spotify 上拥有超过 50 000 名月度听众。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他的热门歌曲《le jeu》累计播放量近2百万次。在这支MV中，我们已经能看到这位蒙特reuil年轻音乐人的一些作品密码。曾经如雨般落下的羽毛，在这里化作行李箱里的羽毛。这个赋予艺人名字的“天使”主题依然令人印象深刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ange 将于 12 月 11 日在巴士帕拉丁（Bus Palladium）举办音乐会。", "links": [{"text": "Bus Palladium", "url": "https://shotgun.live/fr/events/ange-au-bus-palladium"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "欢迎关注我们", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Une pièce vide, un faux plafond et un halo de lumière presque liturgique… Avec “pour te ramener à moi”, l’artiste qui écrit tous ses titres en minuscules a vu les choses en grand pour le premier extrait de son EP attendu en fin d’année.

ange et son réalisateur Gaz ouvrent leur clip sur un tableau de solitude, révélateur de la suite. Autour de l’artiste (sa cigarette toujours fourrée entre ses doigts), ce qui a tout l’air d’un hôtel vide se peuple peu à peu de protagonistes tourmentés. Difficile de ne pas penser à l’Overlook Hotel de Stanley Kubrick dans Shining . Sur des paroles teintées de nostalgie, un homme se rase le crâne face à un miroir, tandis qu’un autre danse avec frénésie. Un corps est étendu au sol, au milieu des confettis et de la fête. Dans le clip, l’enfermement et la libération oscillent.

Des sentiments que porte aussi la musique, à la frontière entre electro, pop et rap de l’artiste, produit par BRUME(s), label qui accompagne d’autres artistes comme Jolagreen et Roninia. Né dans une chambre d’ado, nourri des codes du rap en collectif, avant de bifurquer vers un style plus hybride, ange compte aujourd’hui plus de 50 000 auditeurs mensuels sur Spotify.

Son hit « le jeu » cumule près de 2 millions d’écoutes. On retrouvait déjà dans ce clip quelques codes de la musique du jeune Montreuillois. Là où des plumes tombaient en pluie, on en retrouve ici dans une valise. Le leitmotiv de l’ange qui a donné son nom à un artiste qui reste en tête.

ange sera en concert au Bus Palladium le 11 décembre.

title_original: ドキュメンタリーの秀作を特集上映　山形国際映画祭の受賞作などを都内で  名匠・小川紳介監督らが関わった「幻の作品」も再構成して公開   11月27日まで
editorial_title_zh: 聚焦纪录片佳作 山形国际纪录片电影节获奖作品等在东京上映 名导小川绅介等参与的“梦幻作品”经重新剪辑后公映 持续至11月27日
editorial_excerpt_zh: 展映去年举办的“山形国际纪录片电影节”参赛作品等的专题影展“纪录片梦想秀 山形in东京2026”正在东京都内举行。该电影节于1989年作为亚洲首个真正意义上的纪录片

"credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展映去年举办的“山形国际纪录片电影节”参赛作品等的专题影展“纪录片梦想秀 山形in东京2026”正在东京都内举行。该电影节于1989年作为亚洲首个真正意义上的纪录片电影节创办，在山形市内隔年举办。其特点在于由热爱电影的市民等支撑运营，汇聚了来自世界各国的多元主题作品，国际关注度很高。（照片均由山形国际纪录片电影节提供）", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "去年秋季电影节获奖作品等 "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/0bd5bbcefdb7f0ec68c13b791bf146df.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "比特姆斯基导演专题中上映的《德国影像》 ⒸDeutsche "此次专题展备受瞩目的，是记录了通过市民参与而实现的该电影节首届举办及此前筹备等情况的“梦幻作品”的上映。该电影节的策划得到了曾以展现县内风貌的《日本国古屋敷村》在柏林电影节上荣获国际影评人费比西奖的纪录片巨匠、已故导演小川绅介的深度参与。小川导演向当地的年轻电影爱好者发出号召，诞生了由市民志愿者组成的“YIDFF（山形国际纪录片电影节）网络”，并支撑了运营。世界各国的纪录片导演等齐聚山形的首届电影节盛况等，由长期担任小川作品副导演的饭塚俊男导演将其总结为官方纪录片《电影之都》，并在1991年的第二届电影节上上映。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/eedcf31dbe71fde81607c71488206e54.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "作为首届官方纪录片的《电影之都 山形国际纪录片电影节’89》。台上左侧为小川绅介导演", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "此次在都内上映的除了官方纪录片《电影之都》外，还有将当年饭塚导演拍摄但未公映的粗剪版影像进行数字化、并重新剪辑的作品《电影之都YIDFF网络物语》。据说饭塚导演最初曾构想将市民志愿者的活跃作为《电影之都》的主线，但未能全部容纳。作品捕捉到了已故小川导演热烈阐述电影节意义的场面，以及为该地区前所未有的国际盛会而奔走的志愿者的活跃身影。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artexhibition.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/0df2571a874889fb1105d042085f9507.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "《电影之都 YIDFF网络物语》。传达了由市民参与实现的首届电影节的蓬勃活力", "credit": "美術展ナビ", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "从首届起便参与该电影节运营的桝谷秀一（现YIDFF网络代表、认证NPO法人山形国际纪录片电影节理事）回顾称：“小川从一开始就说，如果不仅靠行政，没有喜欢电影的当地人的参与，电影节是无法成长起来的，为此他播下了种子。至今仍因当地人引以为豪，才使得这一电影节作为在国内外受到评价的活动延续至今。”他还表示：“希望通过让许多人看到这份珍贵的纪录，能够传达小川及当时年轻人们对电影的心意与热忱。”该作品将于11月12日在雅典娜法语文化中心上映，紧随官方纪录片《电影之都》以及将包含小川导演拍摄场面的珍贵影像数字化的作品《Mirror Works ‘89 山形市中央公民馆》之后，桝谷等电影节相关人士还将举办对谈活动。详情请咨询Cinematrix（03-5362-0671），官方网站（https://cinematrix.jp/dds2026/）。（古泽由纪子）", "links": [{"text": "https://cinematrix.jp/dds2026/", "url": article_text:
昨年開催された「山形国際ドキュメンタリー映画祭」の出品作などを特集上映する「ドキュメンタリー・ドリーム・ショー 山形ｉｎ東京２０２６」が東京都内で開かれている。同映画祭は１９８９年、アジアで初の本格的なドキュメンタリー映画祭としてスタートし、山形市内を会場に隔年で開催。映画好きの市民らが運営を支えてきたのが特徴で、世界各国から多様なテーマの作品が集まり、国際的な注目度も高い。（写真はいずれも山形国際ドキュメンタリー映画祭提供）

昨年秋の映画祭の受賞作など 社会派・骨太の作品目立つ

東京での上映は東京の新宿Ｋ’ｓシネマで６日まで開かれたのに続き、１２日まで御茶ノ水のアテネ・フランセ文化センター（８、９日休館）で、１４日～２７日には再び新宿K‘ｓシネマで開催される。 出品作には社会派の骨太の作品が目立ち、１１月１０日には、インターナショナル・コンペティション部門で１３００本を超える応募作からロバート＆フランシス・フラハティ賞（大賞）に選ばれた「ダイレクト・アクション」（ギヨーム・カイヨー、ベン・ラッセル監督作品）が上映される。フランスの農村部を拠点に環境破壊に反対する社会活動家集団に密着した作品だ。６～７日には、同映画祭の審査員を務めたことがあり、昨年死去したドイツの名匠、ハルトムート・ビトムスキー監督がナチス時代の映像記録で構成した「ジャーマン・イメージ」などの作品が上映される。

「市民参加型」映画祭の歩みを記録 トークイベントも

今回の特集で注目されるのは、市民の参加で実現した同映画祭の初回開催とそれまでの準備などの様子を記録した「幻の作品」の上映だ。映画祭の企画には、県内を舞台にした「ニッポン国古屋敷村」がベルリン映画祭で国際批評家連盟賞を受けたドキュメンタリー映画の巨匠、故・小川紳介監督が深く関わった。小川監督が地域の映画ファンの若者らに呼びかけて、市民ボランティアによる「ＹＩＤＦＦ（山形国際ドキュメンタリー映画祭）ネットワーク」が生まれ、運営を支えた経緯がある。世界各国からドキュメンタリー映画の監督らが山形に集まった初回の映画祭の模様などは、小川作品の助監督を長く務めた飯塚俊男監督による公式記録「映画の都」としてまとめられ、１９９１年の第２回映画祭で上映された。

都内で今回上映されるのは、公式記録の「映画の都」のほか、当時飯塚監督が撮影したものの未公開となっていたラフカット（粗編集版）の映像をデジタル化し、再構成した作品「映画の都YIDFFネットワーク物語」。飯塚監督は当初、市民ボランティアの活躍を「映画の都」の主軸として構想していたが、収めきれなかった経緯があるという。作品には、在りし日の小川監督が映画祭の意義について熱弁を振るう場面や、地域で前例のない国際的なイベントに向けて奔走するボランティアたちの活躍が捉えられている。

初回から同映画祭の運営に携わってきた桝谷秀一さん（現・ＹＩＤＦＦネットワーク代表、認定NPO法人山形国際ドキュメンタリー映画祭理事）は「小川さんは当初から、行政だけではなく、映画の好きな地元の人が関わらなければ映画祭は育たないと言って種をまいた。今も地域の人たちが誇りに思ってくれることで、国内外で評価される映画祭として続いている」と振り返る。「多くの人に貴重な記録を見てもらうことで、小川さんや当時の若者たちの映画への思いや熱量を伝えられれば」と話している。 この作品は11月12日、公式記録の「映画の都」、小川監督の撮影場面を含む貴重な映像をデジタル化した作品「ミラーワークス‘８９ 山形市中央公民館」に続いてアテネ・フランセ文化センターで上映され、桝谷さんら映画祭関係者によるトークイベントも開かれる。 詳細はシネマトリックス（03-5362-0671）、公式サイト（ https://cinematrix.jp/dds2026/ ）。（古沢由紀子）

article_text:
With the hope of catching Modigliani momentum evident at auctions in Europe over the past couple years, Phillips is bringing a rare sculpture by the Italian-born modernist to the marquee New York sales in November with a hefty price tag.

Modigliani’s Tête (1911–12) will hit the block with a $28 million–$35 million estimate. If it sells, the sculpture will be one of the most expensive three-dimensional works ever sold at auction by the artist, who is best known as a painter of female nudes with almond-shaped eyes. Related Articles At the Fall's First Major Auctions, Buyers Spent Carefully but Competed for the Right Works Strong Hong Kong Evening Sales, Totaling a Combined $223.6 M., Mask Key Hurdles in Asia's Art Market

The sculpture belongs to a larger series of heads, examples of which are generally held by major institutions, from the Metropolitan Museum of Art to the Tate museum network. This one was carved from a block of limestone and features a slender face with a long nose and a tiny, smiling mouth.

Modigliani is thought to have produced around 28 sculptures during his short lifetime. Twenty-six of them survive.

Calling Tête a “masterpiece,” Phillips deputy chairman of the Americas and senior international specialist Jeremiah Evarts said in a statement, “Fresh to the market after over half a century in the same important private collection, Tête embodies everything that makes Modigliani’s sculpture so revered, including its profound art historical importance.” (The house did not identify who had previously owned the work, which last changed hands in 1972.)

Tête is not likely to become the most expensive Modligiani sculpture ever sold, however. In 2010, Christie’s sold another stone head for $52.8 million, in what was then Modigliani’s overall record. The same auction house sold another Tête in 2019 for $34.3 million.

Modigliani’s current record, it is worth noting, is far higher than the upper end of Phillips’s estimate for its Tête . That benchmark stands at $170.4 million, as minted by the 2015 sale of his 1918 painting Nu couché , which remains one of the most expensive artworks ever brought to auction .

Still, Phillips is likely hoping to catch a wave of market interest in Modigliani evident in auctions staged over the past two years. In 2025, at Christie’s in Paris, a portrait by the artist sold for $31.3 million, tripling its estimate and setting a new record for the artist in France. Then, earlier this year, a painting of a nude woman from the collection of Joe Lewis sold for $63.5 million at Sotheby’s in London, creating a new record for Modigliani in Europe.

editorial_excerpt_zh: 《治愈之旅——纪念9·11》和数百万人一样，我和妻子在电视直播中震惊而难以置信地观看了这场灾难……本文《查克·费希曼》最先发表于《摄影之眼》杂志。

article_text:
Come Healing – Commemorating Sept. 11

Like millions of people, my wife and I watched in shock and amazement, on live TV, the catastrophe taking place on September 11, 2001. I chose to stay home and wait for our son to return from school, not knowing when that might be. When he returned, we asked him what he knew before turning the TV back on. We then drove up a nearby mountain with a long distance view of Manhattan and joined others who had gathered to see the smoke from the destroyed Twin Towers drift over the city skyline. That’s when I began to photograph, telling my son that he would always have pictures of himself the day the world changed. The pictures in this portfolio are all related to that day as witnessed in memorials and commemorations over the next several years.

[{"type": "paragraph", "text": "“You Can See Everything” 票房表现依旧强劲，在上映第二个周末从 2,655 家影院斩获了惊人的 1950 万美元——与其庞大的首映规模相比，门票销量实现了显着增长。", "links": [{"text": "You Can See Everything", "url": "https://variety.com/t/you-can-see-everything/"}, {"text": "from its sizable opening", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/box-office/you-can-see-everything-box-office-nathan-fielder-elizabeth-holmes-huge-start-1236915640/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A24 关于 Theranos 诈骗犯伊丽莎白·霍姆斯的这部备受瞩目的纪录片目前在本土已斩获 4510 万美元票房，在 700 万美元的紧凑预算下，该片将为制片厂带来非常丰厚的回报。凭借极具号召力的口碑、颁奖季的讨论度，以及试图理清银幕所见之事的观众们的反复观影，这部电影在秋季有望继续成为大银幕上的吸金石。它即将以有史以来票房最高的非音乐类纪录片之一的身份下映，对于一部时长近三小时、直到在电影院上映前一个月才进行宣传的电影来说，这无疑是一项真正的壮举。目前，“Michael Jackson’s This Is It” 以 2009 年 2.67 亿美元的票房成为有史以来票房最高的纪录片（未根据通货膨胀进行调整）。与此同时，迈克尔·摩尔的《华氏 9/11》是最大的非音乐纪录片，2004 年票房达 2.22 亿美元，紧随其后的是两部自然电影，2005 年《帝企鹅日记》票房 1.27 亿美元，2007 年《地球》票房 1.07 亿美元。“You Can See Everything” 需要在海外市场大获成功，才能跻身前五名。", "links": [{"text": "A24", "url": "https://variety.com/t/a24/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Variety 热门内容", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/HD-10Oct-CeremonieOuverture-@LoicBENOIT-1248.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "

", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "托德·海因斯、章子怡和丹尼尔·布鲁尔携手星光熠熠的卢米埃尔电影节开幕式，海因斯并抢先透露由佩德罗·帕斯卡主演的《De Noche》", "links": [{"text": "Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/film/global/todd-haynes-pedro-pascal-donald-trump-thierry-fremaux-1236908024/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在北美度过强劲的第二个周末后，以下是《你可以看到一切》意外成功的四个启示。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "克制推高了需求", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "A24最初选择在855家影院上映《你可以看到一切》，对于纪录片来说，这是一个相当大的规模。（相比之下，Bleecker Street在四个地点上映了探讨全球首富的四小时纪录片《马斯克》。）由于影迷们争先恐后地涌入影院以防剧透，该片首映周末斩获1,560万美元票房，这得益于超过2,000场售罄的放映；这部带有“现实比小说更离奇”色彩的故事讲述了霍姆斯因欺诈投资者而即将开始服刑11年刑期之前的生活。事实证明，选择中等规模上映——而不是在少数几个场馆限量上映，或是在2,000多块银幕上全国大规模上映——是非常明智的决定，因为该制片厂既能提高知名度，又能营造出一种稀缺感。（如果你没有提前很久买好座位，想在纽约和洛杉矶的首映周末看到这部电影，那就祝你好运吧。）随后，随着《你可以看到一切》在第二个周末将上映影院扩大到2,666家，门票销量飙升了28%，这凸显了该片在东西海岸之外真正的商业可行性。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“将《你可以看到一切》在855家影院上映是一个非常聪明的举措，让这部电影在更大规模铺开之前能够立足并积累势头，”Rentrak的市场趋势负责人保罗·德尔加拉贝迪安（Paul Dergarabedian）表示。“我们看到一部纪录片在第二个周末能带来如此显著的增长，这确实非同寻常。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "围绕项目的保密工作推高了期待值", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在9月初于特柳赖德电影节上惊艳首映之前，没有人知道《你可以看到一切》的存在。（这在好莱坞简直是个奇迹，在这里甚至连你的服务员都知道你的宣传发行开支。）在这个风景如画的科罗拉多山城，这部电影在收获近乎狂热的评论后，成为了口碑爆款。将电影笼罩在神秘之中成了一种有效的营销策略。毕竟，关于霍姆斯的电影和电视节目并不短缺。她的崛起与戏剧性的陨落已被改编成由阿曼达·塞弗里德主演的Hulu剧集《辍学生》，以及吉布尼的《发明家：硅谷大追捕》。但人们对《你可以看到一切》的直观感受是，联合导演内森·菲尔德和兰斯·奥本海姆捕捉到了非常非常不同的东西。（许多人觉得，霍姆斯终于遇到了她的对手——以HBO的《排练》闻名的尴尬喜剧大师菲尔德。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“请记住，这个项目在开始时没有任何关于如何讲述这个故事的蓝本或剧本，”出版票房通讯 FranchiseRe 的分析师大卫·A·格罗斯（David A. Gross）表示。“A24投资了一个有趣但复杂、且没有开头、中间或结尾的想法。这已经演变成一部关于金钱、梦想、真理和现实的时代精神电影。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "口碑推高了电影第二个周末的票房", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《你可以看到一切》在第二个周末飙升，是因为其品质与热度相称。据民调显示，约90%的初始购票者表示会“强烈推荐”该片，80%的人表示该片“比预期还要好”。在社交媒体上，看过电影的人纷纷鼓励其他人去寻找座无虚席的影院，以便与他人共同分享故事中疯狂的反应和疯狂的转折。从《迈克尔》到《着迷》再到《奥德赛》，今年许多票房大热的作品都有一个共同点：与人群一起观看充满乐趣。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "年轻观众全面支持A24出品的电影资金项目与美学方向，对此全情投入A24的怀抱，拥抱其品牌理念与独特风格（此处结合原文精炼意译，保留核心含义）。年轻观众对A24情有独钟", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "首映周末约有 70% 的购票观众年龄在 35 岁以下，对于一部非虚构电影而言，这是一个出乎意料年轻的观众群体。然而，对于 A24 来说这并不令人意外，多年来，该公司通过《至尊马蒂》和《瞬息全宇宙》等前卫、充满美感的艺术电影，培养了忠实的年轻粉丝群体。今年该独立制片厂推出的《戏剧》、《后室》和《黄金时段》在 Z 世代中达到了活动级别的热度，同样取得了不俗的成绩。但这并不意味着他们会为 A24 的任何作品买单。克里斯·洛克以好莱坞为背景的悲喜剧《Misty Green》以及休·杰克曼的颠覆性冒险片《罗宾汉之死》是 A24 最近在院线失利的两部作品。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
“ You Can See Everything ” has remained a must-see at the box office, collecting a remarkable $19.5 million from 2,655 theaters in its second weekend — a notable increase in ticket sales from its sizable opening .

A24 ‘s buzzy documentary about Theranos fraudster Elizabeth Holmes has grossed $45.1 million domestically to date and will be very profitable for the studio against a lean $7 million budget. With electric word-of-mouth, awards chatter and repeat viewings from audiences who are trying to make sense of what they saw on screen, the movie should remain a big-screen draw through the fall. It’s primed to leave theaters as one of the biggest non-musical documentaries of all time, a true feat for a nearly three-hour film that wasn’t publicized until a month before debuting in cinemas. Right now, “Michael Jackson’s This Is It” is the highest-grossing documentary ever with $267 million in 2009, not adjusted for inflation. Meanwhile Michael Moore’s “Fahrenheit 9/11” is the biggest non-music doc with $222 million in 2004, followed by two nature films, “March of the Penguins” with $127 million in 2005 and “Earth” with $107 million in 2007. “You Can See Everything” needs to become a hit overseas to crack the top five.

Popular on Variety

Related Stories

Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal

After a strong second weekend in North America, here are four takeaways from the surprise success of “You Can See Everything.”

Restraint bolstered demand

A24 began rolling out “You Can See Everything” in 855 theaters, a huge footprint for a documentary. (By comparison, Bleecker Street launched “Musk,” a four-hour look at the world’s richest man, in four locations.) The film opened to $15.6 million — thanks to the more than 2,000 sold-out showings — as cinephiles rushed to theaters to avoid spoilers; the stranger-than-fiction story follows Holmes right before she begins her 11-year prison sentence for defrauding investors. The decision to launch the movie in moderate release — rather than limited in just a handful of venues or nationwide on more than 2,000 screens — proved wise because the studio was able to bolster awareness while cultivating a sense of scarcity. (In New York City and Los Angeles, good luck catching the film during its first weekend in theaters if you didn’t buy a seat way in advance.) Then ticket sales climbed by 28% as “You Can See Everything” expanded to 2,666 theaters in its second weekend, underscoring the film’s genuine commercial viability beyond the coasts.

“Opening ‘You Can See Everything’ in 855 theaters was a really smart move, allowing the film to establish itself and build momentum before going much wider,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian. “The fact that we’re seeing a documentary deliver such a significant second-weekend increase is remarkable.”

Secrecy around the project dialed up the anticipation

Nobody knew about the existence of “You Can See Everything” until its surprise world premiere at the Telluride Film Festival in early September. (That’s nothing short of a miracle in Hollywood, where even your waiter knows your P&A spend.) In the scenic Colorado mountain town, the movie became a word-of-mouth sensation after garnering near-euphoric reviews. Shrouding the film in secrecy became an effective marketing tactic. After all, there’s no shortage of movies and television shows about Holmes. Her rise and spectacular fall from grace has been depicted in the Hulu series “The Dropout,” starring Amanda Seyfried, as well as Gibney’s “The Inventor: Out for Blood in Silicon Valley.” But the immediate sense around “You Can See Everything” was that co-directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had captured something very, very different. (And many felt that Holmes had met her match in Fielder, a cringe comedy master best known for HBO’s “The Rehearsal.”)

“Bear in mind, the project started with no blueprint or screenplay for how to tell this story,” says analyst David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “A24 invested in an interesting but complicated idea without a beginning, middle or end. That’s turned into a zeitgeist film about money, dreams, truth and reality.”

Word-of-mouth elevated ticket sales in the movie’s second weekend

“You Can See Everything” surged in its second weekend because there was quality to match the hype. Some 90% of initial ticket buyers say they would “definitely recommend” the film and 80% said the movie was “even better than expected,” according to exit polls. On social media, people who saw the movie were encouraging others to seek out packed theaters so they could share in the wild reactions and insane twists and turns of the story with others. From “Michael” to “Obsession” to “The Odyssey,” there’s been at least one commonality between many of this year’s box office hits: They’re fun to watch with crowds.

Younger audiences are all in on A24

Roughly 70% of opening weekend ticket buyers were under 35, an unexpectedly youthful turnout for a non-fiction film. However, it’s not surprising for A24, which has cultivated a loyal, young demographic over the years through edgy, aesthetic arthouse favorites like “Marty Supreme” and “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” This year’s lineup of “The Drama,” “Backrooms” and “Primetime” also scored for the indie studio after reaching event-status for Gen Zers. That’s not to say they’ll show up for anything from A24. Chris Rock’s Hollywood-set dramedy “Misty Green” and Hugh Jackman’s revisionist adventure “The Death of Robin Hood” were two recent releases from A24 that misfired in theaters.

article_text:
Spending on Japanese anime worldwide reached a record JPY4.45 trillion ($28.2 billion) in 2025. That is up 15.8% on the previous year, and overseas consumers now account for well over half of the total.

Hasegawa Masahiro, editor-in-chief of the Association of Japanese Animations’ (AJA) annual “Anime Industry Report,” presented the preliminary figures Friday at TIFFCOM , the market attached to the Tokyo International Film Festival . The final numbers will appear in the 2026 edition of the report when it is published in December.

Related Stories

Shabana Azmi, Marco Müller Set for Inaugural Kathmandu Film Festival

Rishab Shetty’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Epic 'The Pride of Bharat' Lands T-Series, Set as Two-Part Saga (EXCLUSIVE)

The rate of growth was also a record, edging past the 15.7% posted in 2024. Overseas revenue climbed 17.2% to JPY2.54 trillion ($16.1 billion), while the local market grew 14.1% to JPY1.91 trillion ($12.1 billion). The overseas share of the total rose to 57.1% from 56.5% a year earlier.

Much of the gain came from home. Local growth was 4.6% in 2024, based on revised figures for 2023, while overseas growth slowed from the 26% recorded that year.

For years, a sluggish home market sat alongside rapid growth abroad. Hasegawa said 2025 broke that pattern, with both sides growing strongly. Overseas revenue first overtook local revenue in 2023, and the gap has widened every year since. He cautioned that exchange rates and global conditions affect the comparison. He added that the overseas total reflects a range of market factors, not only how well individual titles travel.

The AJA measures the business two ways. The broad figure estimates what consumers spend on everything connected to anime, from TV, film and streaming to merchandise, music and live events. A narrower measure tracks revenue earned by animation studios themselves. That studio figure rose 8.4% to a record JPY505.5 billion ($3.2 billion), a slightly slower pace than the 9.1% growth of 2024.

Overseas business made up 27.9% of studio revenue, up from 25.5% in 2024. Studios do not always deal directly with international partners, Hasegawa noted, which keeps that share relatively low.

“The idea of studios holding the rights to their own works and managing them to generate revenue is growing year by year,” he said.

Hasegawa pointed to Japanese titles placing high at the box office in various territories and on global streaming charts. “Just last week, I saw a report that a Japanese anime was No. 2 globally,” he said. “I believe the breakthrough has truly been achieved.”

Japanese anime make up 100 of the 300 TV series with the most user votes on IMDb, including nine of the top 20. “Attack on Titan” leads the ranking with 726,000 votes, ahead of “Rick and Morty.” “Death Note” is No. 3 and “One Piece” No. 9. The other Japanese titles in the top 20 are “Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood,” “ Demon Slayer ,” “One-Punch Man,” “Naruto Shippuden,” “Jujutsu Kaisen” and “Hunter x Hunter.”

The data feeds into a government target for content exports of JPY20 trillion ($126.9 billion) in overseas sales by 2033, with anime expected to contribute JPY6 trillion ($38.1 billion). Japanese content earned JPY6.1 trillion ($38.7 billion) abroad in 2024, and anime accounted for roughly one-third of that.

In the report’s survey, studios listed two priorities for growth markets: localization fitted to local language, culture and law, and anti-piracy measures.

At home, Hasegawa said, anime has long worked as a driver for related content, goods and services. Abroad, it has so far succeeded mainly as something to watch, and the next phase is selling merchandise and services to fans worldwide. He singled out family anime, which is recognized across generations in Japan, as a category whose wide reach at home could become merchandising sales abroad.

“By taking the structure that has been built up in Japan overseas, I believe we can grow toward the JPY6 trillion target,” Hasegawa said.

Ishikawa Kazuko, who heads both the AJA and Nippon Animation, opened the session.

“Above all, it is essential that we build a better environment in which the creators who make the works, and everyone involved in production management, can devote themselves to creating with peace of mind,” Ishikawa said.
